evidence.title: Q59: what Rabreau and Droguet add on models
evidence.summary: Nothing here proves a print filiation, so Q59 stands. In favour of print use: the Beijing libraries held the Cabinet du Roi plates and Pozzo's treatise, which Castiglione is said to have translated (his own claim), and Rabreau sets a Pozzo capital next to the plates, Droguet a Dal Re view of a villa theatre (1743) next to the perspective walls, with Fischer von Erlach and Kleiner in notes. Against a simple filiation: every one is an analogy, by Droguet's own method; Rabreau points out that the Dal Re view has clipped hedges and an arcade screen, not painted walls; he finds no ground for Beurdeley's Trianon or Fontainebleau. Period voices: Delatour's Borromini is style talk from the plates. The Jesuit letters give no description of the buildings (Rabreau).

evidence.title: Plate XX: 线法墙 Xianfa Qiang and 方河 Fanghe
evidence.excerpt_other: Il faut remarquer à l'entrée de la rue, les deux grandes portes placées sur le premier plan.
evidence.summary: The east end of the ground; two rows of houses forming a street, leading the eye to far mountains, cut off from the park by a wide water; two rustic Tuscan gates in the foreground. Called fit for a stage set.

evidence.title: Engraving 20: 线法墙 Xianfa Qiang (湖东线法画) and 方河 Fanghe
evidence.excerpt_other: To produce an illusion of distance by means of the European idea of perspective with a single central vanishing point houses were partly modeled and partly painted on walls, five on each side, set like the wings of a stage,
evidence.summary: A European town seen across a lake: five walls a side narrowing towards the back, with a city wall and mountains painted on the back wall. Plate p.159: the ruin of those walls. Note Q35 has six a side.

evidence.title: 圆明园五朝御制诗文集注 v4, editors' note on 西洋楼
evidence.summary: The editors walk the strip from west to east with completion dates and plaques: 谐奇趣 1751, 养雀笼 1759, then the fountains and the perspective walls, with their mechanical details. They put the whole at about 2% of the gardens.

evidence.title: Plan du theatre d'eau, Lei family archive (线法墙 plan with marked dimensions and laid-down elevations)
evidence.locator: S603 p.124, note 11: Shu Mu et al., Yuanmingyuan ziliao ji, Beijing 1984, p.83
evidence.summary: Durand: this Lei plan gives the walls' positions and low elevations, shows the plate's decor and is credible, so he used it to redraw the walls; 金勋's walls cannot make a perspective effect. Second-hand; likely the same as E0993.

evidence.title: 西洋楼区域考古勘探报告
evidence.locator: mhymy 档案史料 12205, free part
evidence.summary: Report's opening: the strip runs 860 m east-west, up to 300 m wide in the west and 65 m at its narrowest, about 70,000 m2, built 1747-1783. A central axis divides it into about five sections, each with its own north-south axis, thirteen units from 谐奇趣 to 线法墙. Survey results are paywalled.

twins.name: 倦勤斋 通景画 及 小戏台 Juanqin Zhai trompe l'oeil theatre, Qianlong Garden
twins.tells: How 线法 looked when it survives: painted wings, single vanishing point, an illusion of distance
twins.basis: S412 p.38, pp.44-45: both are retirement-garden stages in the far corner of their gardens, perspective by the Jesuits or their Chinese students; Juanqin looks on a painted landscape. S412 p.43: Nian Xiyao's 视学 closely follows Pozzo. S415 p.101: Pozzo as Castiglione's master by his own words.

twins.name: Pozzo, Gesù altar of St Ignatius Altar of St Ignatius, Il Gesù
twins.relation: Comparable: same court, era or type
twins.tells: Panel count at XY15, rail pattern at XY06/XY08
twins.basis: S412 p.43: Pozzo's altar scheme in six painted panels and his treatise; six panels at our stage; Pozzo's book stood in the Jesuit library in Beijing. S415 p.120 uses the same altar's rail as a common source for balustrades here and in Vienna.
